251.t: Illness on the road and stolen trunks
251.s: Henry 'Nick' Turner fell ill in Ashland, Kentucky and the undertaker nearly buried him; Gibson recalls seven trunks of uniforms stolen in Austin and the Thomasville wrecking of instruments.
251.q: That's another question. It's hard for me to answer. I don't remember anybody getting sick, but one time was Turner, wasn't it? What about that? Well, that was in later years. But Henry Turner got real sick in a little town of Ashland, Kentucky, I think. It was in the hills. And we had to...no, I'm…

903.t: Missed bus from Columbia and string of road accidents
903.s: He tells of chasing a Greyhound eight miles, a bus with bad tires, and several car wrecks, including one into a barbershop.
903.q: So all the other people, they wanted to get on ahead of us, so the bus driver told them and said no, so let these musicians get on first because if it don't be for him, none of us would have got home, see, we'd have turned over, you know, off the highway. So we got in the bus and sit down and put…

58.t: Truck fire between Dothan and Birmingham
58.s: Punch tells how the band's truck caught fire and they lost money, clothes and instruments including a mouthpiece.
58.q: when i used to play you know in chicago for honos i had one my because i don't know what kind of that mouthpiece see this i could unscrew this off and put another piece on it like a symbol when your lip was getting tired yeah what about that fire night no i said we were leaving from uh dothan…

215.t: The Vaughn Monroe bus fire in West Virginia
215.s: The bus brakes caught fire, the bus burned down, and the band reached the theater by Greyhound without uniforms.
215.q: Well you know we had the brakes fixed on the bus. And somehow in hot weather, if you used them too soon they explode — not explode, they expand. And we were in West Virginia and we were going up and down and up again and all of a sudden one of the trumpet players in the back, Sleet, said, “Hey…

527.t: Roy Porter's band and the car accident in Hobbs, New Mexico
527.s: A short tour with Roy Porter's band including Eric Dolphy ended in a car wreck.
527.q: With Jay McShann? No, I didn’t go to Phoenix that time. Later on, after I had been in California, Roy Porter organized a band – Roy Porter is a drummer [that] used to play with McGhee – he had organized a band. I would say really it was primarily a rehearsal band. Eric Dolphy was in the band.…

224.t: His drums stolen on the road with Lester Young, 1948
224.s: A man hanging with Pres took his drums in a snowstorm and vanished, so he borrowed a drummer's kit in Cincinnati.
224.q: So the guy that was roadie – he wasn’t roadie. He was just working for Pres that night, hanging with Pres, trying to get the gig to go to California, which he knew about. He put me in a taxi, took my drums. I caught a cold that night, because I was out there waiting in the snow. I’m living 149th…

108.t: The bus with no brakes in Iowa
108.s: The band's used bus loses its brakes near Storm Lake and is saved by the driver Joey's strength.
108.q: They had a bus. He had a bus. He had a lady friend who was quite wealthy. She bought a bus for the band. She bought a bus. It was an old – it had been – it was an American Flyer, or something like that. It was All-American Bus Company or something. She bought a used bus from them. We used to use…

80.t: Stuff Smith sold him a record machine; the rattlesnake in the Alphonso Trent car
80.s: Years earlier in Washington Stuff conned him into buying a disc recorder, and told of a snake thrown into the Trent band's car in Texas.
80.ch: Hopkins, the South and Stuff Smith
80.q: Uh, trying to think, oh, gosh. I -- because I know -- I knew Stuff -- I'm trying to figure -- because I met Stuffy years ago, in Washington, D. C., when I was living in Washington, I was working at the Howard Theater. 'Cause he sold me a recording, a -- an apparatus there, machine.

87.t: Leaking buses, bad jumps and driving accidents
87.s: He rested a month before Barnet; he describes long jumps, Russell Bowles's accident, and Chu Berry's death.
87.q: No, I -- I rested for a month or two, you know. Barnet wanted me to go directly in, but I didn't do it. I was tired, just worn out, you know. We were full of cold from leaking buses out there in the winter and freezing

27.t: The bus burns in Portsmouth, Ohio
27.s: In April 1934 the band bus burned while they ate; the bass and drums were lost but the music and clothes were saved by the driver.
27.q: : We came in there to play a dance, and we parked our bus in the back of a restaurant, so we get our rooms. We were getting rooms. So while we was there eating...

452.t: The weekend in Providence before the crash
452.s: Cobb and his wife drive their new DeSoto with baby Lisette to Providence's Celebrity Club, scouting entertainers, and stay an extra day.
452.ch: On the road, James Brown and the 1956 crash
452.q: All righty -- let me first tell you how I got there. My wife and I were sitting up back on Friday night. She called me Hoss -- that's another one of my nicknames.

387.t: Monitor system, rented instruments and the harp
387.s: His brother built a monitor system; the truck overturned in Vermont.
387.q: My brother made a monitor system so that we could--he designed the thing and set it up for us. He built it because we had no money and he laid out the money and did it. We could not afford it otherwise. We didn't know how that was going to work either. He did it in such a way that it would just…

98.t: Earl Hines's bus accident and road dangers
98.s: They recall the 1935 crash that killed Cecil Irwin, with Lester Young filling in, and the cost of touring today.
98.ch: Changing styles, the road and nightlife
98.q: But those were the conditions with the bands in that time, and they -- all of the band and all of the musicians, black musicians, it wasn't too, too, kosher

13.s: Wilson tells of two bus crashes, the first killing Cecil Irwin and the second sending the bus down an embankment.
13.q: I'm trying to think when the first accident happened. I forgot the year. I think it was '35. We was in Iowa, traveling from Des Moines, Iowa to Minneapolis, open a theater engagement.
